title: Data Observability: Stay Ahead of Issues

scenes.line1: How do you catch data issues early?
scenes.say: How do you spot data pipeline issues before users complain? That's where data observability comes in.

scenes.label: Freshness
scenes.sub: Tracks when data was last updated.
scenes.say: First up, freshness. This tracks when your data was last updated, so you know if you're working with the latest info.

rows.b: Counts rows to spot drops or spikes
Flags changes to columns or types

scenes.say: Other key metrics? Volume counts rows to catch sudden drops. Schema checks for unexpected changes. Distribution looks for weird patterns in the data.

scenes.title: Freshness Check
scenes.say: Picture this: a freshness check pings you if yesterday's sales data hasn't landed by eight in the morning. You catch issues fast.

scenes.question: Is uniqueness a data observability metric?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it's a core observability metric.
scenes.right: Nope. Uniqueness is a data quality dimension, not an observability metric.
scenes.say: Watch out: uniqueness is a data quality dimension, not a direct observability metric. Don't mix them up in interviews.
